entities.summary:
Gerard Geldenhouwer (1482-1542), also known as Gerardus Noviomagus, was a pivotal Dutch humanist, historian, and an early, fervent advocate for the Protestant Reformation in the Low Countries. His intellectual contributions spanned theology, historiography, and political polemic during a period of intense religious and political upheaval. By bridging the critical scholarship of humanism with the emerging tenets of Protestantism, Geldenhouwer became a significant, though often underestimated, figure in the dissemination of reformist thought and the shaping of early Dutch historical consciousness across Northwestern Europe.

Born in Nijmegen, Geldenhouwer initially pursued an ecclesiastical career, serving as secretary to Philip of Burgundy, Bishop of Utrecht, from 1515 to 1524. This position granted him access to influential intellectual and political circles, where he engaged with prominent humanist scholars such as Erasmus. His profound conversion to Protestantism around 1526 marked a decisive turning point, leading him to abandon his Catholic ecclesiastical path and dedicate himself to the Reformation. He subsequently lectured on theology at the University of Marburg and published numerous influential tracts, including his groundbreaking 'Historia Batavica' (1530), a foundational work for Dutch national history.
